benchmark.category: a travel-logging and digital-passport web app with an interactive 3D globe
benchmark.users: travellers recording the countries, cities, trips and photos they have visited, tracking how much of the world they have explored, and sharing their passport and galleries

requirements.source_phrase: Registro mediante correo electrónico y contraseña.
requirements.statement: A visitor at /sign-up registers with an email and password and lands signed in on Inicio with their own empty profile, avatar placeholder and 0,0 % explored

requirements.source_phrase: Registro mediante correo electrónico y contraseña.
requirements.statement: The signup endpoint creates a user with a stable unique id and one profile owned by that id; a second registration with the same email is refused and creates no second user or profile
requirements.notes: paranoid form of 'register': the duplicate registration must be refused by the store, not only by the form

requirements.source_phrase: No esta en la lista el pais de Gibraltar.
requirements.statement: In the country picker opened by the «+ Añadir país visitado» button on the Mi Mundo screen, typing 'Gibraltar' lists Gibraltar with its flag, and selecting it, entering a visit date and saving marks Gibraltar as visited on screen without a reload
requirements.notes: User's own words: Gibraltar is missing from the country list. Kept at the user's granularity -- it must be selectable and it must save -- without narrowing which other entries the list holds.

requirements.source_phrase: No esta en la lista el pais de Gibraltar.
requirements.statement: GET /api/countries returns Gibraltar with its ISO code GI, its name and flag so the picker can list it, and the save call stores a Gibraltar visit owned by the signed-in user rather than dropping it
requirements.notes: The picker can only offer what the country source holds; the demo user's own 195-based list must gain Gibraltar.

requirements.statement: After Gibraltar is saved, a GET of that user's visited countries from a new session returns exactly one Gibraltar record with the visit date that was entered
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the stated fix: the entry must be stored, not only echoed by the picker or kept in browser state.

requirements.statement: Saving Gibraltar again when it is already marked visited does not create a second visit record, and the user's visited-country total for GI stays 1
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'a record can be created': the second identical creation is refused by the store.

requirements.source_phrase: Cuando amplio el mundo se ve borroso y quieor que se vea como la segunda imagen.
requirements.statement: On the Mi Mundo globe, driving the camera to window.__miMundoGlobe.pointOfView({lat:42.5,lng:12,altitude:0.25}) renders coastlines, country borders and the sea as a detailed image for that zoom level, not as an enlarged blurred or blocky version of the world-view image
requirements.notes: The user names the symptom (blurry when zooming in) and a reference image; the testable part is that close-up imagery is rendered from a source at least as detailed as the zoom, sharp enough to read borders around Italy.

requirements.statement: GET /api/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg returns status 200 with a non-empty image/jpeg body for every zoom level from z=2 through z=12, including tiles covering Italy
requirements.notes: Derived from the build description (server-rendered tiles in /app/backend/tiles.py used by WorldGlobe.jsx): the sharpness the user asked for is delivered by real imagery existing at higher zoom levels, not by upscaling one world image.

requirements.source_phrase: Que conforme voy ampliando el mundo se vean los colores en 4k
requirements.statement: Zooming the globe from world view down to altitude 0.25 keeps each visited country filled with its own flag colours at the sharpness of the surrounding imagery, the fill staying inside that country's borders and never turning into a blurred patch or a flat blue block
requirements.notes: The user wants flag colours legible at high zoom, not only a coloured blob at world view; test with a visited country whose flag colours are distinctive (e.g. Italy or Spain).

requirements.statement: A tile requested with the visited codes parameter (?v=CODES) fills the visited countries inside their borders with their flag pattern and leaves unvisited countries dark, returns a valid non-empty image/jpeg, and differs from the same tile requested with no codes
requirements.notes: Derived from the build description: /app/backend/tiles.py renders flag fills server-side so the globe can stay sharp; the tile is the mechanism behind the user's 4K colour request.

requirements.source_phrase: que salgan los nombres de las ciudades donde he estado en la posición correcta donde se encuentra
requirements.statement: Zoomed in on the globe, every city the signed-in user has visited shows a label with that city's name rendered as [data-testid=globe-city-label] at the city's own latitude and longitude, so a city at 41.90,12.50 sits on Rome and not on another country
requirements.notes: Correct position is the testable core; the label's styling is left open.

requirements.statement: Every city saved through the world city search stores its latitude and longitude, and the cities endpoint returns those coordinates for the owner, returning null for a city with no coordinates so it is not placed on the globe
requirements.notes: Derived: a label can only land in the right place if the stored city record carries coordinates from the world city search the user chose in the earlier round.

requirements.statement: Once Gibraltar is saved, the «Mis países» list shows it with its flag, name and visit date and Mi pasaporte shows a Gibraltar stamp, both still present after a page reload
requirements.notes: Derived: the user's complaint is that Gibraltar is absent from the list, so the fix must land in the list and in the passport like any other visited place.

requirements.statement: After Gibraltar is saved the world-explored percentage still equals visited UN countries divided by 195 times 100 rounded to one decimal and is unchanged by the save, while Gibraltar is counted in a separate territories count that the statistics payload returns
requirements.notes: Identity rule: a territory visit is a different kind of entity from a UN-member country visit. The brief's fixed 195-country denominator (193 members plus 2 observers) is the earlier explicit rule and must not be broken by admitting Gibraltar; territory visits are reported separately.

requirements.statement: GET /api/countries also returns other non-UN territories the app stores (for example Hong Kong, Puerto Rico, Greenland), each with its ISO code, flag and a territory marker, so the fix is not hardcoded to Gibraltar alone
requirements.notes: Guards against narrowing the user's complaint to one row: the list must be complete for territories, not patched for GI only.

requirements.statement: After Gibraltar is saved as visited, the globe no longer leaves it in unvisited grey: at close zoom it carries its flag colours or a flag pin at its location, and it is listed among the user's visited places
requirements.notes: Derived: visited countries change colour when registered, so a newly admitted territory must be reflected on the globe as well as in the list.

requirements.statement: Clicking a city label on the globe navigates to /ciudades/:id for that city and the page shows that city's name, its country and its photos
requirements.notes: Derived from the build description (labels are [data-testid=globe-city-label] and navigate to /ciudades/:id); the label must lead to the city it names, not to a neighbouring city.

requirements.statement: GET /api/cities/{id} for a city owned by the caller returns that city's own name, country and visit dates, and a request for a city belonging to another account is refused with none of its fields returned
requirements.notes: The label's target page must read the right record and refuse a guessed id belonging to another user.

requirements.statement: Zooming out to world view removes the city labels, and zooming back in to altitude 0.25 shows each visited city's label exactly once, not duplicated and not left floating over the ocean
requirements.notes: Paranoid state check for a control that is operated repeatedly: the label layer is rebuilt, not stacked.

requirements.statement: The globe shows city labels only for the signed-in user's own cities: after signing out and signing in as the second demo account, none of the first account's city labels remain on the globe
requirements.notes: Something private stays private: city labels reveal where a person has been, so they must follow the session, not a cached response.

requirements.statement: The cities endpoint returns only cities owned by the caller with their coordinates, and a query naming another user's id returns none of that user's cities, not even their names or counts
requirements.notes: Tenant/account boundary on the label data path; enforced on the server, not only by hiding the label layer.

requirements.statement: Typing a partial, differently-cased query such as 'gib' or 'GIBRALTAR' in the country picker still lists Gibraltar among the matches
requirements.notes: benchmark: travel-logging apps let a traveller find a country by typing a few letters, case- and accent-insensitively; a list that only matches a full exact name would make Gibraltar nominally present but still effectively missing for the user who reported it.

requirements.statement: Repeating a zoom-in and zoom-out cycle ten times on the globe keeps one label per visited city and one globe instance, and a fresh pointOfView still answers about as fast as the first, with no steadily growing tile request count
requirements.notes: Performance and leak class applied to the zoom fix: the new high-zoom rendering must not leak layers, timers or duplicate requests each time the user zooms.

requirements.statement: A repeated request for the same tile returns the same image bytes and responds faster than the first request for that tile, whose first render completes in roughly a second rather than timing out or returning an error
requirements.notes: Derived from the build description and misc notes: tiles are fetched upstream from ESRI World Imagery on first request (~0.5s) and cached afterwards, which is what keeps repeated zooming responsive.

requirements.statement: On the Mi Mundo globe, clicking directly on a tiny country such as Gibraltar or Vaticano at close zoom opens that country's own information panel with its name and flag, not the panel of the larger country around it
requirements.notes: From the developer agent's iteration-2 report ('Clicking near a tiny country without click polygon (Gibraltar, Vaticano) opens that country instead of the surrounding one') and the brief's 'Al pulsar sobre un país se abrirá una ventana con su información'. The user's Gibraltar complaint makes a country that cannot be clicked still effectively missing; hard to test because the click target is a 0.5-degree polygon inside a much larger neighbour.

requirements.statement: GET /api/countries/{code} for GI or VA returns that country's own name, flag and the caller's visited status for it, and an unknown code is refused with a not-found response rather than a neighbouring country's record
requirements.notes: The globe panel can only show the clicked country if the endpoint resolves that exact code; derived from the same iteration-2 report as the frontend requirement.

requirements.statement: In the «Añadir ciudad» city search box, typing a query and then clearing the field removes the spinner and any stale result list and leaves the box idle, and when the city lookup fails the screen shows an error message instead of an endless spinner or a silent empty list
requirements.notes: From the developer agent's iteration-2 report ('clearing input resets spinner; upstream errors surface as error'), which realises the user's earlier choice of a 'Buscador mundial de ciudades'; the failure path is what a browser test must observe.

requirements.statement: GET /api/cities/search?q= resolves the query through the world city service with its key read on the server and returns matching cities with name, country and latitude/longitude; an empty q returns an empty list immediately, and an upstream failure returns an error the screen can show rather than an empty success
requirements.notes: Derived from the build report; the coordinates it returns are what the globe city labels depend on, so a swallowed upstream error would also silently drop city labels.

requirements.statement: A flag image that fails to download while a tile is being rendered is not cached as a permanent failure: repeating the same tile request tries that flag again, and the flags for all visited countries on one tile are fetched in parallel so the tile still responds in roughly the time of a first render rather than the sum of its flags
requirements.notes: From the developer agent's iteration-2 report ('failed flag downloads are no longer cached; flags fetched in parallel'); this is the mechanism behind the user's 4K flag-colour request, and a cached failure would leave a visited country grey forever.

requirements.statement: Opening a share link for a city or gallery in a signed-out browser shows that city's name, its shared photos and description and none of the owner's private content, still after a reload
requirements.notes: From the developer agent's iteration-2 report of the public-view fix, realising the brief's 'Compartir la ciudad o galería mediante un enlace' and 'Privado por defecto' starting state.

requirements.statement: GET on the public share endpoint for a token returns only the shared city's allowed fields (name, country, description and the photos the owner shares), carries no owner share token, email or unshared photo, and an unknown or revoked token returns nothing of the record
requirements.notes: From the developer agent's iteration-2 report ('share_token stripped in public_view'); a public payload that echoes the owner's token or unshared photos is a privacy leak the browser view alone cannot rule out.

requirements.statement: PATCH /api/cities/{id} validates the submitted visit dates against the stored dates and the proposed cover photo against the stored gallery before moving any photo, so an invalid update is refused whole and the stored city, its photo list and its cover are unchanged
requirements.notes: From the developer agent's iteration-2 report ('city update validates dates against stored values and cover before moving photos'); the paranoid form of 'an action succeeds' — the failure path must leave nothing half-written.

requirements.statement: On startup the backend ensures the unique indexes it relies on, so two identical visits for the same user and country submitted at the same time leave one stored record and the second submission is refused
requirements.notes: From the developer agent's iteration-2 report ('startup awaits unique indexes'); complements the duplicate-visit requirement by making the store itself refuse the race, not only a pre-check.

unmapped_phrases.reason: operational continuation message from the session, carries no product requirement
